title: Modals & Obligation
objective: Use must, have to, should, can, might and their negatives without mixing up the meanings.

sections.heading: Obligation: must / have to
sections.body:
`must` and `have to` both express strong obligation: `You must wear a seatbelt.` `I have to work on Saturdays.`
`mustn't` = prohibition (do not do it!): `You mustn't use your phone in the exam.`
`don't have to` = no obligation (you can if you want, but it is not necessary): `You don't have to pay — it's free.`
sections.bodyZh: must 与 have to 都表示强烈义务；mustn't 表示禁止（千万别做）；don't have to 表示没有必要（不必做）。

examples.en: You mustn't smoke in the hospital.
We don't have to wear a uniform at my school.

sections.tip: mustn't ≠ don't have to. This pair is tested in almost every PET paper. Prohibition vs no obligation.

sections.heading: Advice: should / ought to
sections.body:
`should` gives advice or opinion: `You should see a doctor.` `He shouldn't eat so much fast food.`
`ought to` has the same meaning but is less common: `You ought to arrive early.`
sections.bodyZh: should 提建议或看法；ought to 意思相同但较少用。

examples.en: You should drink more water when you do sport.
I think she should take the job.
examples.zh: 我觉得她应该接受那份工作。

sections.tip: In Writing Part 2, should/shouldn't is perfect for giving advice in articles.

sections.heading: Possibility & ability: can, could, might, may
sections.body:
`can` = ability or permission: `I can swim.` `Can I open the window?`
`could` = past ability or polite request: `She could read when she was four.` `Could you help me?`
`might/may` = possibility (maybe): `It might rain later.`
sections.bodyZh: can 表示能力或许可；could 表示过去的能力或礼貌请求；might/may 表示可能性（也许）。

examples.en: Take an umbrella — it might rain this afternoon.
examples.zh: 带把伞——今天下午可能会下雨。

examples.en: Could you tell me the way to the station?
examples.zh: 你能告诉我去车站的路吗？

sections.tip: For polite requests in Speaking, prefer Could you...? / Would you mind...?

sections.heading: Modals + perfect (extension)
sections.body: Stronger students may meet `must have / can't have + past participle` for past deduction: `He must have forgotten.` `She can't have left already.` You do not need to produce these at B1 — just recognise them in Reading.
sections.bodyZh: 程度较好的学生可能在阅读中遇到 must have / can't have + 过去分词，表示对过去的推测。B1 阶段只需认读，不需主动使用。

examples.en: The lights are off. They must have gone out.
examples.zh: 灯都关了。他们肯定出门了。

sections.tip: Recognise it, don't worry about producing it.

commonErrors.wrong: You don't have to smoke here. (meaning prohibition)
commonErrors.why: don't have to = no obligation; mustn't = prohibition.
Modals are followed by the bare infinitive, without to.

keyPoints: must / have to = obligation · mustn't = prohibition · don't have to = not necessary.
can = ability/permission · could = past ability/polite request · might = possibility.
Modals take the bare infinitive (no to).
